VAL-CROSS-001.evidence: Verified through integration test 'Cross-role handoff flow > worker handoff feeds evaluator and dispatcher in sequence' in handoff-flow.test.ts (line 608) which tests worker→evaluator→dispatcher data flow in sequence. Also verified through issue-gating.test.ts 'cross-role chain: handoff → evaluator → stage context → dispatcher > non-blocking issues from evaluator flow into stage context for next dispatcher' (line 686-774) which runs a full 2-phase execution loop confirming: (1) evaluator issues from phase 1 accumulate into stage context, (2) stage context with cumulative_issues is passed to the dispatcher for phase 2. Source code inspection confirms: execution-loop.ts line 598-618 builds evaluatorHandoff from cached worker handoff (including warnings, decisions) and passes stageContext to evaluator.evaluate(). Line 619 passes stageContext to evaluator. Line 750/1030 passes stageContext to dispatcher. dispatcher-orchestrator.ts line 38/92 accepts and forwards stageContext. EvaluatorInputSchema (evaluator.ts line 35) has stage_context field. DispatcherInputSchema (dispatcher.ts line 68) has stage_context field.

VAL-CROSS-001.observations: All 37 handoff-flow tests pass (0 fail). The cross-role chain test specifically verifies the end-to-end flow: evaluator non-blocking issues → stage context accumulation → dispatcher receives cumulative_issues. Source wiring confirmed in execution-loop.ts (evaluatorHandoff construction at line 598, stageContext passed to both evaluator at line 619 and dispatcher at lines 750/1030), dispatcher-orchestrator.ts (stageContext parameter at line 38), and schema definitions (EvaluatorInputSchema.stage_context, DispatcherInputSchema.stage_context).

VAL-CROSS-002.evidence: Verified through multiple tests in issue-gating.test.ts: (1) 'blocking issues halt pipeline > halts pipeline when evaluator returns blocking issues even with passed:true' — confirms blocking issues halt pipeline even when evaluator says passed:true. (2) 'blocking issues surface via approval gate > calls requestIssueApproval with blocking issues' — confirms requestIssueApproval is called with the blocking issues array and the user sees issue descriptions. (3) 'blocking issues surface via approval gate > continues pipeline when user approves blocking issues' — confirms pipeline resumes after user approval (runs phase 2 after approving phase 1 blocking issues). (4) 'blocking issues surface via approval gate > halts pipeline when user rejects blocking issues' — confirms pipeline halts when user rejects. Source code inspection confirms: execution-loop.ts lines 798-854 implement issue gating — blocking issues are filtered, surfaced via approvalHandler.requestIssueApproval(), and pipeline halts or continues based on approval result.

VAL-CROSS-002.observations: All 18 issue-gating tests pass (0 fail). The full chain is covered: evaluator returns blocking issues → execution loop detects them → requestIssueApproval called with issue descriptions → user approval/rejection determines pipeline continuation. The test at line 587 also verifies that non-blocking issues accumulate in stage context while blocking ones trigger the gate — matching the specification that 'the evaluator classifies one as a blocking issue, the execution loop halts and surfaces the issue through the approval gate'.

VAL-CROSS-005.evidence: Verified through dedicated tests in issue-gating.test.ts: (1) 'stage context feeds evaluator > evaluator for phase N receives cumulative stage context from prior phases' (line 589) — runs 2-phase loop, confirms second evaluator call has stage_context defined with phase_count >= 1. (2) 'stage context feeds evaluator > first phase evaluator gets no stage context (empty or undefined)' (line 637) — confirms first evaluator call has no stage_context or phase_count === 0. Source code inspection confirms: execution-loop.ts line 619 passes `this._stageContext.phase_count > 0 ? this._stageContext : undefined` to evaluator.evaluate(), and line 898 calls accumulatePhaseIntoContext() after each phase completes. EvaluatorInputSchema (evaluator.ts line 35) has optional stage_context field using StageContextSchema. StageContext (stage-context.ts) accumulates decisions, warnings, artifacts, and issues per phase.

VAL-CROSS-005.observations: Both stage-context-feeds-evaluator tests pass. The evaluator for phase N receives the cumulative stage context from phases 1 through N-1, verified by checking evalTransport.calls[1].stage_context is defined with phase_count >= 1. The first phase evaluator correctly receives no stage context (undefined or phase_count === 0). The accumulation logic in stage-context.ts is a pure function that grows the context immutably per phase, including cumulative_decisions, cumulative_warnings, cumulative_artifacts, cumulative_issues, and skill_feedback — all available for the evaluator to reference when assessing the current phase.
